children: Ola Electric Mobility shares jumped 8 percent in afternoon trade on August 31, extending their gains from the previous session, as sentiment around the electric two-wheeler maker remained buoyant following the launch of its new mass-market S1Z scooter range.

The stock climbed to Rs 42.1, emerging as the top midcap gainer for the day. With Monday's surge, Ola Electric shares have gained around 11.3 percent so far in 2026, compared with a 7.5 percent decline in the Nifty 50. The company's market capitalisation rose above Rs 19,300 crore.

The gains came amid a combination of positive developments around Ola Electric and the broader electric two-wheeler market, including the company's recent S1Z launch and a Rs 95.8-crore incentive sanctioned under the government's Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme.

Ola Electric shares had gained 3.2 percent on Friday after the company unveiled the S1Z, its new mass-market electric scooter range featuring its indigenously developed Bharat Cell LFP battery technology. The 3.1 kWh and 5.1 kWh variants have been priced at an introductory Rs 79,999 and Rs 99,999, respectively, with claimed IDC ranges of up to 179 km and 301 km.

The latest PLI sanction could also provide some support to the company's cash flows. The Ministry of Heavy Industries has sanctioned Rs 95.8 crore for Ola Electric under the PLI-Auto scheme for FY27, with the amount to be released through IFCI, the central nodal agency.

title: Ola Electric shares jump 8%, extend gains after S1Z launch; PLI incentive, EV demand in focus
